candidates.buyer: Moto-taxi, taxi and minibus drivers and owners in N'Djamena; the SNMT union and urban transport cooperatives as channel
candidates.evidence: https://tchadinfos.com/2026/04/09/ndjamena-la-mairie-accorde-60-jours-aux-transporteurs-urbains-pour-se-conformer-a-la-nouvelle-reglementation/ ; https://tchadinfos.com/2026/06/07/transport-urbain-a-ndjamena-les-nouvelles-mesures-pour-moderniser-et-securiser-le-secteur/ ; the SNMT (national moto-taxi union) was launched Apr 2025: https://tchadinfos.com/2025/04/13/tchad-le-syndicat-national-de-moto-taxi-lance-officiellement-ses-activites/
candidates.existing: Competitor search (local-language query 'application enrolement mototaxis taxis N'Djamena ... plateforme numerique') found no digital enrolment platform in N'Djamena. Enrolment is in person at the Voirie urbaine. Digital enrolment exists only in Douala, Cameroon (2024). Not a state-built system so far.
candidates.name: Moto-taxi and taxi driver compliance wallet, N'Djamena (agrement, municipal ID number, professional card, vest)
candidates.trigger: N'Djamena municipal note of 9 Apr 2026 (60 days, now expired) plus a joint order of the Public Security and Transport ministers: Transport ministry agrement (2026 cost halved), enrolment and ID number at the Voirie urbaine, yellow vest, professional card, vehicle colours and numbers, mixed-force checks; the helmet rule is still under discussion
candidates.unchecked: Agrement fee and form; number of drivers; whether the city plans a digital system; legal basis (joint order number); whether enforcement actually happened; drivers' ability to pay; smartphone use among drivers

candidates.buyer: Owners of several moto-taxis or minibuses, and transport cooperatives, in N'Djamena
candidates.existing: Not searched separately; same competitor search as C01 found none.
candidates.known_note: Sibling of C01; could be merged.
candidates.name: Fleet owners' document tracker for taxis, minibuses and moto-taxi fleets (owners who rent vehicles to drivers)
candidates.trigger: Same 2026 N'Djamena rules, plus carte grise and registration checks from the 2025 circular; vehicles must carry visible ID numbers and colours
candidates.unchecked: Whether multi-vehicle owners are numerous; renewal cycle of the agrement

candidates.buyer: Owners of two- and four-wheeled vehicles, small dealers of used vehicles
candidates.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers / 33
candidates.name: Vehicle regularisation helper (carte grise, customs clearance, tinted-window authorisation)
candidates.trigger: Circular N005/PR/PM/MSPX/SG/2025 of 27 Mar 2025: regularisation window 3-24 Apr 2025 (extended to 9 May 2025) for unregistered vehicles, fake carte grise, uncleared vehicles, unauthorised tinted windows
candidates.unchecked: Whether a new window is announced; this was a one-off with expired deadline; mostly individuals, not businesses

candidates.buyer: Founders and directors of private schools (about 1,025 in 2023, 140 unauthorised then)
candidates.existing: Competitor search (logiciel gestion ecole privee Tchad ...) found no state platform for authorisation files and no approved school-management tool; only an old 2021 classifieds ad for a generic school-management program.
candidates.name: Private school authorisation and teacher-contract compliance pack
candidates.trigger: Moratorium on new private schools lifted by PM arrete of 4 Nov 2025 with stricter conformity checks and closure threat; circular of 10 Jul 2026: only state-recognised diploma holders, CDI contracts, pay at least SMIG, checks at the next school-year start
candidates.unchecked: Exact authorisation checklist and fees; no recurring report found, so frequency is low; teacher diploma verification; willingness to pay by small schools

candidates.name: Private health-training school authorisation tracker
candidates.trigger: Health ministry circular of 9 Sept 2025 against illegal opening; provisional or definitive authorisation required
candidates.unchecked: Number of schools; recurring duties; fee

candidates.buyer: Livestock traders, market operators, hide and skin exporters
candidates.known_note: Hides, sesame and groundnut share the export-duty rule with gum arabic (K03) but different buyer groups.
candidates.name: Livestock trader sales-tax and export-duty paperwork (cattle and camel sale tax, hides export duty, 2028 live-export ban)
candidates.trigger: 2025 Finance Law: sale tax on cattle and camels raised 2,000 FCFA (+33%); arrete 6 Aug 2025: 5% export duty plus 2% statistical fee on hides, gum arabic, sesame, groundnut; circular of 31 Jul 2026 prepares ban on live-animal exports from 1 Jan 2028
candidates.unchecked: Collection mechanism at markets; vet certificate procedure; who files; traders mostly informal and cash

candidates.buyer: Gold buyers, transporters and site managers; artisanal miners (324 gold sites in 2024)
candidates.known_note: Competitor check not run in budget.
candidates.name: Gold buyers and artisanal miners authorisation tracker (SONEMIC one-stop window)
candidates.trigger: SONEMIC due to run a one-stop window for authorisations to buy and sell gold and precious metals, artisanal mining, processing, site management and transport; special mining brigade; prospecting authorisations suspended 11 Sept 2026
candidates.unchecked: Whether the window is live; per-transaction reporting; buyers' count; security and informality of sector

candidates.buyer: Local associations (4,600+ recognised); about 100 new requests monthly in 2023
candidates.known_note: K02 targets NGOs for FEN and tax withholding, not registration.
candidates.name: Association and NGO compliance (authorisation under Ordonnance 023/PR/2018, dissolution risk)
candidates.trigger: Ordonnance 023/PR/2018: declaration then ministerial authorisation within 3 months; dissolutions by arrete (5 Jan 2026 for two associations); no periodic report duty confirmed
candidates.unchecked: Annual filing duties; low willingness to pay; political sensitivity

candidates.buyer: Private security companies in N'Djamena and their client firms
candidates.known_note: Same core duty (CNPS declarations) as K05.
candidates.name: Private security guard firms: CNPS declaration and labour inspection compliance
candidates.trigger: Employers must declare workers to CNPS; labour inspectors and CNPS controllers can sanction; union complaint Sept 2025 of no social protection; Labour Code law 6/PR/2015
candidates.unchecked: Licensing regime for security firms; enforcement strength

candidates.buyer: Importers and retail dealers of pesticides and fertilisers
candidates.name: Agro-input dealers (pesticides and fertilisers) licensing and register
candidates.trigger: Decree 011/PP/MA/99 (national pesticide control commission) and CILSS common regulation; producers in Mandoul (Oct 2024) call for enforcement
candidates.unchecked: Whether the commission works; dealer register; reporting duty; the rule seems unenforced

candidates.buyer: Licensed bureaux de change (SA or SARL, 50M FCFA capital)
candidates.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
candidates.name: Money-changer (bureau de change) CEMAC licence and reporting
candidates.trigger: Regulation 02/18/CEMAC/UMAC/CM and BEAC Instruction 011/GR/2019; BEAC sanctions for foreign-exchange breaches
candidates.unchecked: Number of Chadian bureaux; reporting forms and frequency; probably too few buyers

candidates.name: Fuel retailers: ARSAT jerrycan-sale cap and authorisation records
candidates.trigger: ARSAT note limiting jerrycan sales to 60 L per day without ARSAT authorisation (stated in a search summary of a tchadinfos item; date and text not opened); butane import authorisations late 2025
candidates.unchecked: Source not opened; licence regime; whether sales records must be kept; the rule is crisis-driven

candidates.existing: Not checked; no pharmacy software or state price database found in search.
candidates.known_note: Competitor search not run for lack of budget.
candidates.name: Pharmacy wholesaler and retailer price-label and storage compliance
candidates.trigger: Health ministry circulars of 10 Sept 2025: public prices must appear on supply invoices and boxes, sanctions from temporary closure to licence revocation; second circular on storage norms for medicines and lab reagents; inspection mission of private pharmaceutical establishments from 17 Feb 2025
candidates.unchecked: Whether a national price list or portal exists; count of pharmacies; whether pharmacies already use local software; inspection frequency

candidates.buyer: Notaries, bailiffs, auctioneers, liberal professionals and projects invoicing public bodies
candidates.evidence: https://europe.thomsonreuters.com/fr/compliance/regulatory-updates/chad ; https://orbitax.com/news/country/article/Chads-2026-Finance-Law-introd_6e8eb302-225d-11f1-8a90-42f7e08108ee (excerpt only, paywalled) ; https://www.e-invoice.app/country/TD (snippet only, page blocked 403)
candidates.existing: Competitor search (logiciel facturation FEN Tchad agree DGI ... notaires huissiers) found no list of DGI-approved software and no local vendor. The state FEN portal is free (fen.finances.gouv.td, linked from Orbitax). Global vendors serve large firms (see K06).
candidates.known_note: Different buyer group (small professional offices) than K01 bridge for ERP users, but the core duty (FEN) is the same and the free state portal likely covers it; close to K01 and K02.
candidates.name: FEN invoicing for liberal professions and ministerial offices (notaries, bailiffs, auctioneers) selling to public bodies
candidates.trigger: 2026 Finance Law: from 1 Jan 2026 FEN invoices required for VAT transactions with institutional counterparties and as a condition of processing public expenditure; suppliers must register and use DGI-approved software
candidates.unchecked: Exact scope and penalties in the 2026 Finance Law text; whether the free portal is sufficient for small offices; sources disagree on start date (2023 vs 2026)

candidates.buyer: Chadian freight, transit and forwarding firms
candidates.name: CEMAC regional transport operator agrement filing support
candidates.trigger: CEMAC transport agrement sessions; 12 Chadian files, 9 approved in June 2026; rejection for non-payment
candidates.unchecked: Article suggests the agrement is voluntary; tiny buyer count; filing is occasional

candidates.buyer: SIM sellers and mobile-money kiosk agents

candidates.name: SIM re-identification and mobile-money agent kiosk register
candidates.trigger: ARCEP control of anonymous SIM sales (May 2025) under article 032 of 2023 and operator licence terms
candidates.unchecked: Agent-level duty; whether a register must be kept; pay capacity

candidates.known_note: Could not be checked within the search budget.
candidates.name: Hotel and guest-house registers and tourist levy
candidates.trigger: Not found; search returned only non-Chad sources
candidates.unchecked: Whole category: guest register rule, tourist levy, ministry list of regulated activities

coverage.category: 1. Household employers
coverage.found: Only generic CNPS employee-declaration duty found (tchadinfos 2025/09/29); nothing specific to domestic workers. Nothing new beyond K05.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No search spent; budget used on higher-signal categories.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Via gold search: SONEMIC to create one-stop window for authorisations to buy/sell gold and precious metals (not yet confirmed operational); 324 gold sites (2024); new prospecting authorisations suspended 11 Sept 2026. See candidate C07.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No search spent. Related one-off: 27 Mar 2025 circular on unregistered or uncleared vehicles (C03).

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Cattle/camel sale tax raised 2,000 FCFA (+33%) in 2025 Finance Law; live-animal export ban planned from 1 Jan 2028 (circular 31 Jul 2026); 5% export duty plus 2% statistical fee on hides, gum arabic, sesame, groundnut (arrete 6 Aug 2025). See C06.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Only that abattoirs are under construction ahead of the 2028 export ban; no butcher register rules found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: No vet-specific rule found. STDF notes weak animal-health control and a constraining regulatory framework.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Decree 011/PP/MA/99 (CNCPUA pesticide control commission) and CILSS common rules exist; producers in Mandoul (2024) say the commission is not operational and ask for regulation of imports and sales. No register or reporting workflow found. See C10 (weak).

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: No licensing regime found for placement agencies; private security guards in N'Djamena lack social-security cover (union complaint, Sept 2025). See C09.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies
coverage.found: Associations governed by Ordonnance 023/PR/2018: declaration plus ministerial authorisation within 3 months. More than 4,600 recognised associations (2023). Two associations dissolved by arrete of 5 Jan 2026. No periodic reporting duty found. See C08. No halal/kosher rules found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators
coverage.found: Strong 2026 trigger in N'Djamena: mototaxi, taxi and minibus drivers need a Transport ministry agrement, a municipal ID number, a yellow vest, a professional card and painted vehicle colours. A 60-day deadline from 9 Apr 2026 has passed, and mixed-force checks are announced. A joint order of the Public Security and Transport ministers sets the conditions. See C01, C02.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers: CEMAC Regulation 02/18/CEMAC/UMAC/CM (2018) and BEAC Instruction 011/GR/2019 require SA or SARL with 50M FCFA capital and licensing. No Chad-specific reporting tool found. See C11 (weak).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections
coverage.found: Private schools: moratorium on new private schools lifted 4 Nov 2025; in 2023 only 669 of 1,025 private schools were compliant; circular of 10 Jul 2026 requires diploma-holding teachers, CDI contracts and at least SMIG pay, with checks at the school-year start. Private health-training schools also told to regularise (circular 9 Sept 2025). Driving schools, tattoo studios and nurseries: nothing found. See C04, C05.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Regulator is ARSAT (downstream hydrocarbons). Feb 2026 note caps jerrycan sales at 60 L per day without ARSAT authorisation; butane shortages and extra import authorisations in late 2025. No licence-renewal or reporting workflow found. See C12 (unverified).

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Gum arabic and sesame exports need a special Ministry of Commerce authorisation (more than 10 documents, per an AfCFTA trade-barrier complaint resolved 6 Feb 2025). Export duty of 5% plus 2% statistical fee since arrete 6 Aug 2025. Nothing new beyond K03.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Microfinance is supervised by COBAC/BEAC (regional). No Chad-specific lists or reporting forms found. Mobile-money payment-institution licences were granted in 2025 (Konoom, Moov Money). Unverified.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers
coverage.found: No clinic-licensing or insurer-billing rule found. Pharmacy side is in category 25.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals
coverage.found: 17 Feb 2025: inspection mission of private pharmaceutical establishments in N'Djamena. 10 Sept 2025: two circulars, one on wholesalers respecting public prices (printed on invoices and boxes, with closure or licence revocation as sanctions), one on storage norms. See C03b below, listed as C13.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security guards unprotected by social security (tchadinfos 2025/09/29); CNPS and labour inspectors can sanction. Labour Code is law 6/PR/2015. No agency licensing found. See C09.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: Only mining items: prospecting suspension (Sept 2026), SONEMIC window. Nothing on construction site registers or local-content reports.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals
coverage.found: 2026 Finance Law widens FEN use to associations, NGOs, liberal professions and ministerial offices (notaries, bailiffs, auctioneers) and projects for VAT transactions with institutional counterparties, effective 1 Jan 2026 (Thomson Reuters, Orbitax, e-invoice.app). See C14.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
coverage.found: Search found no Chad rules on guest registers or tourist levy. Unverified.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules
coverage.found: Export duties (arrete 6 Aug 2025) on groundnut, gum arabic, sesame, hides; special export authorisation for gum and sesame. Nothing new beyond K03.

coverage.category: 31. Urban transport municipal agrement and enrolment (N'Djamena, 2026)
coverage.found: Strongest new lead. See C01 and C02.

coverage.category: 32. Private education establishments (authorisation and teacher-contract compliance, 2025-2026)
coverage.found: See C04.

coverage.category: 33. Vehicle and engine regularisation (Public Security circular 005/PR/PM/MSPX/SG/2025)
coverage.found: One-off Apr-May 2025 window for unregistered vehicles, fake carte grise, tinted windows. See C03.

coverage.category: 34. Artisanal and small-scale gold mining and SONEMIC authorisations
coverage.found: See C07.

coverage.category: 35. CEMAC regional transport operator approval (agrement CEMAC for freight and forwarding firms)
coverage.found: 9 of 12 Chadian files approved in June 2026 session; AGL files rejected for non-payment. Appears voluntary and regional; sessions are periodic. See C15 (weak).

coverage.category: 36. Telecom SIM re-identification and mobile-money agent kiosks
coverage.found: ARCEP checked anonymous SIM sales in May 2025 (law/article 032 of 2023 and licence terms). No agent-registration procedure found. See C16 (unverified).

coverage.category: 37. Livestock and hides export taxation and the 2028 live-animal export ban
coverage.found: See C06.
